Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:10:1.english: With an oath - For an unpaid bailee swears that he was not negligent.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:11:1.english: One collects - A debt from the slaves.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:12:1.hebrew: אפי' מיתמי - אם מת לוה ונפלו קמי יתמי, מי א"ר אלעזר דבעל חוב גובה מן העבדים, דכמקרקעי דמו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:12:1.english: Even from orphans - If a borrower died and [his slaves] fell before the orphans, did Rabbi Elazar say that a creditor collects from the slaves because they are like real estate?

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:12:2.hebrew: מיניה - מן הלוה עצמו, א"ר אלעזר דב"ח גובה מן העבדים:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:12:2.english: From him - From the debtor himself, Rabbi Elazar said that a creditor collects [his debt] from the slaves.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:12:3.hebrew: וקפריך מיניה - אפי' מן גלימא דעל כתפיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:12:3.english: And he challenges: "From him?!" - Even from the cloak that is on his shoulders.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:13:1.hebrew: אפותיקי - אפה תהא קאי, כלומר: מזה יהא לך פרעון. ואשמעינן רבי אלעזר דאם מכרו, גובה בעל חוב ממנו:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:13:1.english: Appoteiki [designated repayment] - "On this [property] it shall stand," meaning: from this [property] shall be your payment. And Rabbi Elazar teaches us that if he sold him [the slave], the creditor collects from him.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:1:1.hebrew: דיש מקצת שליא בלא ולד - ודקאסרי לה באכילה, גזירה מקצתה אטו כולה. והאי דקתני סימן ולד לאו אמקצתה קאי, אלא ה"ק: אסורה באכילה גזירה אטו היכא דנפקא כולה, ואתו למימר אין כאן ולד, ואם חזרה לפנים תשתרי בשחיטת האם וקאכלי נבילה, דההיא ודאי סימן ולד באשה כו'. אבל גבי אשה לא ניחוש למקצת לטמא טהרות דראשון, דהתם ליכא למיגזר אטו כולה, דהא קחזי, דמכי נפק ולד בשני מטמינא לה. קמ"ל:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:1:1.english: That there is part of an afterbirth without a fetus - And as for why they prohibit it from being eaten, [it is] a decree [prohibiting] part of it due to [the case of] all of it. And this that [the mishna] teaches, "a sign of a fetus," does not refer to part of it; rather, this is what it is saying: it is prohibited from being eaten [as] a decree due to [a case] where all of it emerged, and they might come to say, "There is no fetus here," and if it went back inside, it would become permitted through the slaughter of the mother, and they would be eating neveila [meat of an unslaughtered animal], for that [whole afterbirth] is certainly "a sign of a fetus in a woman, etc." However, regarding a woman, we should not be concerned about part [of an afterbirth] to render ritually pure items of the first [day] impure, for there, there is no reason to make a decree due to [the case of] all of it, since one sees [when it is all of it], for as soon as the fetus emerges on the second [day], we render her impure. [Therefore, Ulla] teaches us [that part of an afterbirth does not emerge without part of a fetus].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:2:1.hebrew: אין פודין אותו - אין צריך לפדותו. ואם מת מעצמו לא איצטריך לן למימר, דהא כתיב (במדבר יח): "ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה". אבל השתא איצטריך לאשמועי' דלא אמרינן: אי לא איקטיל הוה חי, ולא נפל הוה, וליפרקיה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:2:1.english: One does not redeem him - One does not need to redeem him. And if he died on his own, it was not necessary for us to say [this], for behold, it is written (Numbers 18[:16]): "And those to be redeemed of him, from a month old shall you redeem." But now [that he was mauled], it was necessary to teach us that we do not say: "Had he not been killed, he would have lived, and he was not a non-viable infant, so let him be redeemed."

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:2:2.hebrew: בכור שנטרף - בכור אדם שנהרג בתוך ל' יום:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:2:2.english: A firstborn who was mauled - A human firstborn who was killed within thirty days.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:3:1.english: You shall surely redeem - "Yet you shall surely redeem the firstborn of man" [Numbers 18:15].

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:5:1.hebrew: במסירה תנן - בפ"ק דקדושין, דכיון דמסר לו באפסר, קנאה, אע"פ שלא משכה מרשות מוכר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:5:1.english: By passing, we learned - In the first chapter of Kiddushin, [which teaches] that once [the seller] passed it to him by the halter, [the buyer] has acquired it, even though he did not pull it out of the seller's domain.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:5:2.hebrew: זו וזו - גסה ודקה בהגבהה, וגסה מתרצינן בקדושין שנותן חבילי זמורות תחת רגליה והיא עולה עליהן:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:5:2.english: This and that - [Both] a large [animal] and a small [animal are acquired] by lifting. And [regarding] a large [animal], we explain in Kiddushin that one places bundles of branches under its feet and it climbs onto them.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:6:1.hebrew: מה שעל בניהן ובנותיהן אין שמין - דכיון דבנים ובנות לא אתו לבי דינא, לא מבזינן להו למיתי:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:6:1.english: Whatever is upon their sons and daughters, they do not appraise - For since the sons and daughters do not come to court, we do not humiliate them [by requiring them] to come.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:7:1.hebrew: בגדול אחי - גדול האחין העוסק בנכסים להכניס ולהוציא, דעד השתא ניחא להו לאחין דליכסי מדידהו במלבושים נאים, כי היכי דלשתמעון מיליה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:7:1.english: With the eldest brother - The eldest of the brothers, who deals with the estate to bring in and take out [assets], for until now it was agreeable to the brothers that he be clothed from their [joint property] in fine garments, so that his words would be listened to.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:8:1.hebrew: שומר שמסר לשומר פטור - הראשון, בכל אותן דינים שהיה פטור אם היתה אצלו, פטור נמי השתא, ולא אמרי' פשיעה היא זו שמסרה לאיש אחר:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:8:1.english: A bailee who conveyed [a deposit] to [another] bailee is exempt - The first [bailee], in all those laws in which he would have been exempt had [the deposit] been with him, is also exempt now, and we do not say [that] this is negligence that he conveyed it to another person.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:8:2.hebrew: ולא מבעיא שומר חנם שמסר לשומר שכר - ונגנבה או שאבדה, דפטור שומר חנם, כי היכי דמיפטר אילו הואי גביה, דלא פשע:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:8:2.english: And it is not necessary [to state this regarding] an unpaid bailee who conveyed [a deposit] to a paid bailee - and it was stolen or lost, that the unpaid bailee is exempt, just as he would have been exempt had it been with him, since he was not negligent.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:8:3.hebrew: דעלויי עלייה לשמירתו - דשומר שכר מסר נפשיה לנטורי טפי משומר חנם, שהרי שומר שכר חייב בגניבה ואבידה:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:8:3.english: For he elevated its safeguarding - For a paid bailee exerts himself to guard [it] more than an unpaid bailee, since a paid bailee is liable for theft and loss.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:8:4.hebrew: אלא אפי' שומר שכר שמסר לשומר חנם דהשתא גרעה לשמירתו פטור - שומר שכר באונסין, ולא מצי א"ל בעל הבית: פשעת שמסרת לאחר, שהרי מסרה לבן דעת:
Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:8:4.english: Rather, even a paid bailee who conveyed [a deposit] to an unpaid bailee, thereby decreasing [the level of] its safeguarding, is exempt - [That is,] a paid bailee [is exempt] in [cases of] unavoidable accidents, and the owner cannot say to him, "You were negligent in that you conveyed [it] to another [person]," since he conveyed it to a mentally competent person.

Rashi on Bava Kamma 11b:9:1.english: [He is] liable - Even for unavoidable mishaps.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:10:1.hebrew: את מהימנת לי בשבועה - לפי טעם זה, אם השני נאמן יותר מן הראשון, נראה דפטור; אבל בהמפקיד (שם) איכא טעמא אחרינא: ד"אין רצוני שיהא פקדוני ביד אחר", ואין שני טעמים הללו שוין, כדמוכח התם. ואין להקשות לעולא דהכא: היכי פליג אההוא טעמא, הא מתניתין היא בפ' כל הגט (גיטין כט.): "אם אמר: טול ממנה חפץ פלוני, לא ישלחנו ביד אחר, שאין רצוני שיהא פקדוני ביד אחר"? וי"ל: דההוא לכתחילה, אבל לא מצינו שיתחייב בדיעבד על כך:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:10:1.english: You are credible to me with [taking] an oath - According to this reason, if the second [bailee] is more trustworthy than the first, it appears that [the first] is exempt; however, in [Chapter] HaMafkid (ibid.), there is another reason: "I do not want my deposit to be in the hand of another," and these two reasons are not equivalent, as is proven there. And one cannot ask against Ulla here: how does he disagree with that reason, [given that] it is a Mishnah in Chapter Kol HaGet (Gittin 29a): "If he said, 'Take such-and-such an object from her,' he may not send it by the hand of another, because I do not want my deposit to be in the hand of another"? And one can answer: that [Mishnah] applies initially, but we do not find that he becomes liable after the fact on account of this.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:12:1.hebrew: אפילו מן גלימא דעל כתפיה - אם יש לו שנים, דאם אין לו אלא אחד, הא אמר בפ' המקבל (ב"מ קיד.) דמסדרים לב"ח. א"נ, בטלית ששוה מאה מנה, שמלבישין אותו בטלית הראוי לו, ולא כר"ע דאמר בפ' המקבל (בבא מציעא קיג:): "כל ישראל ראויין לאותו איצטלא". ור"ת פוסק הלכה דאין מסדרין:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:12:1.english: Even from the cloak that is upon his shoulders - [This applies] if he has two [cloaks]; for if he has only one, behold, it is stated in the chapter HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 114a) that we make an assessment [of basic needs to leave] for a debtor. Alternatively, [it refers] to a cloak worth a hundred maneh, where they dress him in a cloak befitting him [and collect the expensive one], and not in accordance with Rabbi Akiva, who said in the chapter HaMekabel (Bava Metzia 113b): "All of Israel are fit for that robe." And Rabbeinu Tam rules as the halakha that we do not make an assessment [for a debtor].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:13:1.hebrew: כגון שעשאו אפותיקי - והשתא גבי מיתמי כמו מלוקח. ואע"ג דמיתמי לא שייך טעמא משום קלא כמו בלוקח, דלגבי דידהו אפותיקי ולא אפותיקי שוה — מכל מקום היכא דגבי מלקוחות גבי נמי מיתמי, מידי דהוה אמלוה בשטר דגבי מיתמי ומלקוחות אפילו למ"ד שיעבודא לאו דאורייתא, ומלוה על פה לא גבי ממשעבדי ולא מיתמי. ובשלמא בלקוחות איכא לפלוגי בין ע"פ לבשטר: דבמלוה בשטר גובה משום נעילת דלת, ובמלוה על פה לא גבי משום דליכא קלא, ובשטר אית ליה קלא; אבל מיתמי, מה לי מלוה ע"פ, מה לי מלוה בשטר? אלא ודאי כל היכא דגבי מלקוחות משום נעילת דלת גבי נמי מיתמי, כמו מלוה בשטר או מלוה הכתובה בתורה למ"ד ככתובה בשטר דמי, או כשעמד בדין — גבי נמי מיתמי; אבל במלוה על פה, כיון דלא חש לעשות שטר לגבות מלקוחות, כי לא גבי נמי מיתמי ליכא נעילת דלת. וה"פ: "א"ר אלעזר אפי' מיתמי" — בלא אפותיקי משום דהוי כקרקע? "לא, מיניה" — פי': בלא אפותיקי לא גבי אלא מיניה. ופריך: מיניה לכול'? ומשני: באפותיקי, וגבי נמי מיתמי ומלקוחות. א"נ: דקרי מיניה אע"ג דגבי נמי מיתמי, כיון דמכח הלוה שעשאו אפותיקי קא גבי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:13:1.english: For instance, where he designated him as an appoteiki [designated repayment] - And now he collects from orphans just as from a buyer. And even though with orphans the reason of publicity [kala] does not apply as [it does] with a buyer, since for them [an] appoteiki and [a] non-appoteiki are the same — nevertheless, wherever he collects from buyers, he also collects from orphans, just like a loan [recorded] in a document, where one collects from orphans and from buyers even according to the one who says that a lien is not biblical, whereas an oral loan is not collected from encumbered [sold] property and not from orphans. Now, granted, with buyers one can distinguish between an oral [loan] and [one] in a document: for with a loan in a document he collects because of [preventing] the closing of the door [to borrowers], whereas with an oral loan he does not collect because there is no publicity, while with a document it has publicity; but from orphans, what is [the difference] to me [between] an oral loan, [and] what is [the difference] to me [between] a loan in a document? Rather, certainly wherever he collects from buyers because of [preventing] the closing of the door, he also collects from orphans — just like a loan in a document, or a loan written in the Torah according to the one who says it is considered like one written in a document, or when he stood in court — he also collects from orphans; whereas with an oral loan, since he did not bother to make a document in order to collect from buyers, when he also does not collect from orphans there is no closing of the door. And this is its explanation: "[Did] Rabbi Elazar say [this] even from orphans" — [meaning,] without [an] appoteiki, because [a slave] is like land? "No, from him" — meaning: without [an] appoteiki, he collects only from him. And he objects: "From him" [etc., i.e., even from the cloak on his shoulders]! And he answers: [It is speaking] of [an] appoteiki, and he also collects from orphans and from buyers. Alternatively: [the reason] it calls [this collecting] "from him" even though he also collects from orphans [is] because he collects by virtue of the borrower who designated him as an appoteiki.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:1:1.hebrew: גזירה מקצתה אטו כולה - לאו דוקא, דאיך נוכל לטעות להתיר כולה? שגם ביציאת מקצתה היוצא אסור מדאורייתא, ולא קאמרינן "גזירה מה שבפנים אטו מה שבחוץ"! ועוד, אי גזרינן אטו כולה, באשה נמי לגזור! אלא י"ל דאטו רובא קאמרינן: דאי שרית ביציאת מקצת מה שבפנים משום "כל אשר בבהמה", אע"פ שיש לחוש שמא יצא ראשו באותו מקצת, יבא להתיר ביציאת רובו אותו מיעוט שבפנים מהאי טעמא, ולא ידעו שבמקצת הוי ספק ספיקא. אבל גבי אשה לא שייך למגזר, דלא אתי למיטעי, דליכא טעמא במה יטעו להשוות רוב למקצת; אבל בבהמה יטעו לומר שמה שבפנים לעולם אינו כילוד כל זמן שלא יצא. א"נ, באשה לא גזרי' למנות מיום ראשון, דחומרא דאתי לידי קולא היא, דדלמא לא ימנו מיום ב' למיהב לה ימי טומאה. א"נ, באשה לא גזרינן, דאפושי טומאה לא מפשינן, כדאמרינן בביצה (דף ז.). מיהו לעיל פירשנו דלא איירי לענין טומאה, אלא לאוסרה לבעלה. ופי' הקונט' דבאשה לא שייך למגזר, דלא אתי למטעי, דכיון דחזו דמכי ילדה בשני מטמינא לה; וקשה, דהא דחזינן דמטמאינן לה בשני, אמרי משום דנפקא כולה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:1:1.english: A decree [prohibiting] part of it due to all of it - [This] is not exact, for how could we err to permit all of it? For even when [only] part of it emerges, that which emerges is forbidden by Torah law, and we are not saying "a decree [forbidding] what is inside due to what is outside"! And furthermore, if we decree due to all of it, let us also decree in [the case of] a woman! Rather, one must say that we mean "due to the majority of it": for if you permit what is inside upon the emergence of a minority [of the afterbirth] because of [the verse] "whatever is in an animal [you may eat]" — even though there is room to be concerned that perhaps its head emerged with that minority — one will come to permit, upon the emergence of the majority of it, that minority which is inside for this [same] reason, and they will not know that in [the case of] a minority [emerging] it is a double doubt. However, regarding a woman, it is not relevant to decree, for they will not come to err, since there is no reason by which they would err to equate a majority with a minority; whereas regarding an animal, they will err to say that whatever is inside is never considered born as long as it has not emerged. Alternatively, regarding a woman, we do not decree to count from the first day, because it is a stringency that leads to a leniency, for perhaps they will not count from the second day to give her [all her] days of impurity. Alternatively, regarding a woman, we do not decree, because we do not increase impurity, as we say in [Tractate] Beitzah (7a). However, above we explained that it does not deal with the matter of impurity, rather with forbidding her to her husband. And Rashi explained that regarding a woman it is not relevant to decree, for they will not come to err, because once they see that from when she gives birth on the second [day] we render her impure; and [this] is difficult, for [regarding] that which we see that we render her impure on the second [day], they will say [it is] because all of it emerged [then].

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:2:1.hebrew: בכור שנטרף בתוך ל' יום - פ"ה: שנהרג, ובמת מעצמו לא איצטריך קרא לאשמועינן דאין פודין, דהא כתיב: "ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה", אבל נהרג איצטריך לאשמועינן דלא אמרי': אי לאו דאקטיל הוי חי ולא נפל הוי, ולפרקיה. משמע קצת דאם קים לן בגויה דכלו לו חדשיו וחי, היה חייב לפדותו. וקשה, דבפרק יש בכור (בכורות דף מט.) אמר גבי פודה בנו תוך ל' יום ונתאכלו המעות לאחר זמן: אין בנו פדוי. ואמאי? והא אגלאי מילתא למפרע דלא נפל הוא! אלא ודאי גזירת הכתוב היא מ"ופדויו מבן חדש תפדה", דאפי' קים לן שכלו חדשיו צריך ל' יום. ואע"ג דמהאי קרא נפקא לן (שבת דף קלה:) כל ששהה ל' יום באדם אינו נפל, ה"נ דרשינן (שם) ח' ימים בבהמה אינו נפל, מדכתיב: "מיום השמיני והלאה ירצה לקרבן"; ואפ"ה כי קים לן דכלו חדשיו הוי מחוסר זמן תוך שמנה, כדמוכח בפ"ק דר"ה (דף ו:) דאמר: [בכור] מאימתי מונין לו שנה? חד אמר: משעה [שנראה] להרצאה, וחד אמר: משעה שנולד; ולא פליגי — הא בתם, הא בבעל מום; ומוקמינן לה התם דקים ליה בגויה דכלו לו חדשיו, ואפ"ה לא חזי להרצאה עד ח'. ועוד, דבסוף הקומץ רבה (מנחות דף לז.) מחייב גבי בכור שיש לו ב' ראשים ליתן לו י' סלעים לכהן, ופריך עלה מבכור שנטרף דפטור; ואי נטרף היינו נהרג, היכי מדמי ליה להכי? ועוד, דלא הוה ליה למימר "נטרף" אלא "נהרג". ועוד, דאסיק גמרא "אך" חלק — הא כיון שנהרג תוך ל' יום, מ"ופדויו מבן חדש" נפקא! ומפ' ר"ת: שנטרף היינו שנעשה טרפה. והשתא מדמי ליה שפיר בהקומץ לבכור שיש לו ב' ראשים, דהוי נמי טרפה:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:2:1.english: A firstborn who was mauled (nitraf) within thirty days - Rashi explains: [it means] that he was killed; and [in the case of] one who died on his own, a verse is not needed to teach us that we do not redeem [him], for it is written: "And his redemption, from a month old you shall redeem" (Numbers 18:16). However, [for one who] was killed, [a verse] is needed to teach us that we do not say: "Had he not been killed, he would have lived and he is not a non-viable infant, so let him be redeemed." This somewhat implies that if we are certain regarding him that his [gestation] months were completed and he was viable, one would be obligated to redeem him. And this is difficult, for in chapter Yesh Bekhor (Bekhorot 49a), it states regarding one who redeems his son within thirty days and the money was consumed after [that] time: his son is not redeemed. And why? Behold, it was revealed retroactively that he is not a non-viable infant! Rather, it is certainly a scriptural decree from "and his redemption, from a month old you shall redeem," that even if we are certain that his months were completed, thirty days are required. And even though from this verse we derive (Shabbat 135b) that any [child] who survives thirty days among humans is not a non-viable infant, so too we expound (there) that eight days among animals is not a non-viable infant, from what is written: "from the eighth day and onward it shall be accepted for an offering" (Leviticus 22:27); even so, when we are certain that its months were completed, it is still considered premature within eight [days], as is proven in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (6b), where it states: From when do we count a year for [a firstborn animal]? One says: from the time [it is fit] to be accepted [as an offering], and one says: from the time it was born. And they do not disagree — this one [refers] to an unblemished [animal], and that one [refers] to a blemished [animal]; and we establish it there [as speaking of a case] where one is certain regarding it that its months were completed, and even so it is not fit for acceptance until eight [days]. And furthermore, at the end of HaKometz Rabbah (Menachot 37a), [the Gemara] obligates, regarding a firstborn who has two heads, to give ten sela to the priest, and it raises an objection against it from "a firstborn who nitraf," which is exempt; now, if nitraf means "was killed," how could it compare that case to this? And furthermore, it should not have said "nitraf," but rather "was killed" (neherag). And furthermore, the Gemara concludes [that] "yet" (akh) differentiates — but since he was killed within thirty days, it is derived from "and his redemption, from a month old"! Therefore Rabbeinu Tam explains: "who nitraf" means that he became a tereifah [having a fatal physical defect]. And now it aptly compares it in HaKometz to a firstborn who has two heads, which is also a tereifah.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:4:1.hebrew: בהמה גסה - אין עיקר הדבר כאן, ובפ"ק דקדושין (דף כה:) הארכתי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:4:1.english: A large animal - The main [place for this] matter is not here, and in the first chapter of Kiddushin (25b) I have elaborated.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:6:1.hebrew: מה שעל בניהן ובנותיהן אין שמין - שמתביישין להביאם לב"ד ומחלי אהדדי, ופסק רב אלפס: דוקא בגדי חול, אבל בגדי שבת שמין; והכי איתא בירושלמי:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:6:1.english: Whatever is upon their sons and daughters, [the court] does not appraise - because they are embarrassed to bring them to court, and they waive [their claims] to one another. And Rav Alfas ruled: [this applies] specifically [to] weekday garments, whereas Sabbath garments are appraised; and so it is stated in the Yerushalmi.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:7:1.hebrew: בגדול אחי - אם מוחין, הרשות בידם; אבל כל זמן שלא מיחו, מסתמא ניחא להו כי היכי דלשתמעי מיליה, כדאמרינן בהניזקין (גיטין נב:) גבי עמרם צבעא:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:7:1.english: With the eldest brother - If they [the other brothers] object, they have the right [to do so]; however, as long as they have not objected, it is presumably pleasing to them so that his words will be listened to, as we say in [the chapter] HaNizakin (Gittin 52b) regarding Amram the dyer.

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:8:1.hebrew: לא מבעיא שומר חנם שמסר כו' - פי' דפטור אם נגנבה או נאבדה, ומיהו שומר שכר כי משלם, משלם לבעלים, כדאמרי' בהמפקיד (ב"מ לו:), דהלכה כר' יוסי דאמר: "אין הלה עושה סחורה בפרתו של חבירו":
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:8:1.english: "It is not necessary [to state this in the case of] an unpaid bailee who conveyed [a deposit]," etc. - This means that [the unpaid bailee] is exempt if it was stolen or lost. However, when the paid bailee pays, he pays to the owner, as we say in [the chapter entitled] HaMafkid (Bava Metzia 36b), that the halakha follows Rabbi Yosei, who says: "That one [the first bailee] may not do business with his fellow's cow."

Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:8:2.hebrew: דעלויי עלייה לשמירתו - אין לפרש עלייה שאם נגנב תחזור לבעלים, דהא גרועי גרעיה לא אפשר לפרש בענין זה; אלא העילוי והגרעון הוי דשומר שכר מסר נפשו טפי לשומרו משומר חנם:
Tosafot on Bava Kamma 11b:8:2.english: Thereby elevating its safeguarding - One should not explain "elevating [it]" [to mean] that if it is stolen, [compensation] will return to the owner, for "diminishing [it]" cannot be explained in this manner; rather, the elevation and the diminution are that a paid bailee exerts himself more to guard it than an unpaid bailee.
